chunks: Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad said: Abu Abdullah ibn Ghalib, the brother-in-law of Abul Hasan ibn Abi Tayyib, said: I did not see anyone wiser than the Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh. I remember seeing him one day in the house of Ibn Yasar. He had a great position with the Sayyid (the Caliph) and al-Muqtadir. The common people also revered him, and Abul Qasim attended due to dissimulation (taqiyyah) and fear.

I remember two men arguing; one claimed that Abu Bakr was the best of people after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then Umar, then Ali. The other said, 'Rather, Ali is better than Umar.' Their debate intensified. Abul Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'What the companions are unanimous upon is that the Siddiq (Abu Bakr) comes first, then after him the Faruq (Umar), then after him Uthman (Dhu al-Nurayn), then Ali (the Successor). The people of Hadith are upon this, and it is the correct view with us.'

Those present in the gathering were amazed by this statement. The attending common people raised him above their heads (in joy), and there was much supplication for him and criticism of those who accused him of Rafidism. Laughter overwhelmed me; I tried to restrain myself, putting my sleeve in my mouth, fearing exposure. I jumped up from the gathering. He looked at me and noticed me. When I arrived home, there was a knock on the door. I went out quickly and found Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) riding his mule, who had come to me from the gathering before proceeding to his house.

He said to me: 'O Abu Abdullah, may Allah support you, why did you laugh as if to cheer me, as if what I said was not true in your view?' I said: 'It is true in my view.' He said: 'Fear God, O Shaykh, for I will not make you excused if you consider this statement of mine great/strange.' I said: 'O my master, a man who believes he is the companion of the Imam and his representative, saying this statement, is it not awkward and laughable?'
He said to me: 'By your life, if you repeat this, I will desert you.' He bid me farewell and left.

key_terms.تَقِيَّةٌ: Dissimulation or concealment of belief due to fear
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْإِمَامِ: Companion of the Imam (a high-ranking deputy)

ai.seo_question: What did al-Husayn ibn Ruh say about the companions' preference for the Caliphs, and why did the narrator laugh?
ai.summary: This narrative highlights the concept of *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) employed by al-Husayn ibn Ruh, the fourth major deputy of the Twelfth Imam, to maintain communal unity by affirming the Sunni consensus (*Ijma*) of the companions' preference for Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uuthman before Ali. The narrator’s suppressed laughter reveals the tension between the Shia scholarly reality—where this view is often considered correct but secondary to Imam Ali's unique status—and the public expectation of a deputy to assert Ali's superiority. Ibn Ruh’s warning underscores that doubting the validity of this reported consensus, even when it aligns with Sunni tradition, constitutes a breach of faith for the representative of the Imam.
